The Claude Platform in Rings

Anthropic’s platform drawn as five rings around the model: the Messages API, the tool-use loop, the agent harness and the products people use. Each ring turns at its own speed. Hover a ring to hold it still, or tap any block to see what it does and where this site covers it.

Inner rings are closer to the model; outer rings build on everything inside them. The orange ring is one request travelling in to the model and back out.

How the platform works, layer by layer

Each layer is built on the one below it, and the products sit on top.

1 · The models (core)

Opus, Sonnet and Haiku are the trained models. On their own they only take text (and images) in and produce text out: no memory, no tools, no internet. Everything else is built around that.

2 · The Messages API (the doorway)

  • Stateless: every call sends the whole conversation again; the API remembers nothing between calls.
  • Prompt caching: a long, repeated start of a prompt is stored, so later calls are cheaper and faster.
  • Batch: many jobs run in the background at a lower price.
  • Extended thinking: the model reasons in a separate block before it answers.
  • Same models elsewhere: also offered through Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry.

3 · The tool-use loop (giving the model hands)

The model cannot act by itself, but it can ask for a tool:

  1. You describe the tools: a name plus a JSON schema for the inputs.
  2. The model replies, for example: call get_weather(city='Paris').
  3. Your code runs it and sends back the result.
  4. The model continues, perhaps asking for more tools, until it is done.

Some tools Anthropic runs itself (web search, fetching a page, running code in a sandbox); others are your own functions.

4 · The agent harness (running the loop for you)

Writing that loop well is hard: context, permissions, retries, files and sub-tasks all need handling. So Anthropic packages it:

  • Agent SDK: the same loop that powers Claude Code, as a Python or TypeScript library.
  • MCP connectors: a standard way to plug in tools like GitHub, Drive, Jira or your own systems.
  • Skills and hooks: skills are packaged know-how; hooks are your own checks before or after a tool call.
  • Computer and browser use: the model sees screenshots and clicks and types.
  • ⚠️ Hosted agents and scheduled runs: shown in the source figure; exact names and scope not confirmed.

5 · Products (what people use)

  • Claude apps (web, desktop, mobile): model + API + tools such as search, files and memory, with a chat window on top.
  • Claude Code: model + tool loop + harness, pointed at your codebase and terminal.
  • Claude in Chrome: the harness plus browser use, inside your browser.
  • Claude in Slack and office suites: the same pieces, placed where teams already work.
  • Your own app: whatever developers build on layers 1 to 4.
The key idea: the model’s intelligence is the same in every product. What changes is the layers around it: what it can remember, which tools it can use, where it runs and who approves its actions. A request from Claude Code travels in through the harness, the tool loop and the API to the model, then back out the same way; that is the orange pulse on the rings.

⚠️ Managed Agents, Scheduled tasks and M365/Workspace are shown as in the source figure; we have not confirmed their names and scope in Anthropic’s documentation. Rotation speeds are decorative and mean nothing. Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site.
